_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Saturday March 28| 5:37 a.m 

Bonjour Tremblant!

It's the biggest day of the spring season and Tremblant is pumped; our Caribou Cup day is here!!! Welcome to the event that marks the arrival of spring in Tremblant. Come soak up the energy, (hopefully) the sunshine, and everything that makes this tradition so special. Temperatures are starting out cold this morning, so make sure to dress up well and bundle up! The good news is that it should warm up a bit towards the afternoon, just in time for the Caribou Cup festivities. The action kicks off at noon, and there will be a halftime entertainment show at 13h that you won't want to miss. Come cheer on the competitors and be part of the fun!

Conditions are looking fantastic to celebrate: crisp air, groomed runs ready to carve, 4 terrain parks in full swing, and the glades loaded with fresh snow over the past week. Please note that the Porte du Soleil chairlift and the Edge side will be open today, so the full mountain is yours to explore! Additionally, a few runs will open progressively due to variable conditions. 

Whether you're competing, cheering, or just out for a great ski day, today is one you won't want to miss. We'll see you on the slopes!
And to close out this special day on a meaningful note, don't forget that tonight is Earth Hour! From 20h30 to 21h30, we invite everyone to turn off non-essential lights for one hour as a sign of commitment to our planet. Every small gesture counts! 

Mountain safety tip of the week: Safe Behavior in Terrain Parks. It's important to always clear landing zones after using features and never stop in these areas to watch others. All terrain park users must also wear a helmet.

Think Ahead
  • Plan before using each feature; your speed and position will directly affect your takeoff and landing. Visualize your move before you drop in.
Look Before You Leap
  • Inspect features before using them, and continue to do so throughout the day.
  • Wait your turn, make sure the landing is clear before you go, and clear the landing area quickly.
Take It Easy
  • Warm up, start with smaller features, and progress as you improve.
  • Perform tricks within your ability level to stay in control.
  • Take lessons to improve your skills.
Respect the Park and Others
  • Respect the park, other users, the Mountain Code of Conduct (Code de conduite en montagne) and all signage. Respect goes both ways!
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.

All 4 sides of the mountain are open, with freshly groomed runs, 4 terrain parks, and plenty of glade skiing to take advantage of the fresh snow from the past week. Temperatures will be cold in the morning but should warm up towards the afternoon. Tonight, don't forget Earth Hour from 20h30 to 21h30!
_inspectorSnowReport.SafetyReportFrench: Bon samedi! Aujourd'hui c'est la Coupe Caribou! Les festivités débutent à midi avec un spectacle de mi-temps à 13h. Les 4 versants de la montagne sont ouverts, avec des pistes fraîchement damées, 4 parcs et beaucoup de ski en sous-bois pour profiter de la neige fraîche de la dernière semaine. Les températures seront froides en matinée mais devraient se réchauffer en après-midi. N'oubliez pas l'Heure de la Terre ce soir!
